newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese bond futures firm with foreign trend.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese bond futures firm with foreign trend.

text.p: Portuguese bond futures ended firmer with foreign markets and dealers said uncertainties over EMU meant that spreads against 10-year Bunds were unlikely to narrow soon. *June 97 futures up 0.37 points to 108.79 *Feb 07 cash (OTC) 100.45 (100.56), yld 6.55 (6.54) *Spread vs Spanish 10-yr cash -9 bps vs -14 bps cls Fri

Portuguese bonds firmed in line with peripheral markets and dealers said uncertainties over the launch of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) meant that spreads against 10-year Bunds would not narrow soon.
Dealers said the late strength of the escudo was not enough to justify a rate cut by the Bank of Portugal tomorrow.
"The market recovered, pulled by peripheral markets and a conviction that a Socialist government in France will defend the entry of Club Med countries to EMU," said a fixed income analyst.
Some dealers said they doubted that the new French government would keep tight control over the budget, and said concerns over the valuation of German official reserves would continue.
"These two elements jeopardise the (launch of the) euro (in 1999), and this is not good news for peripheral markets," said a dealer.
